_doc: Episode 'Your first plate' (docs/getting-started.md). One entry per scene; each language is a list of sentences (cues). Numbers in words, no exclamation marks. Narrate with the canvas-video skill: narrate.py website/video/first-run

en: From an empty phone to a logged meal, in a few minutes.
Open your instance's address on the phone, over HTTPS.
The encrypted store needs a secure page, so a plain address on your home network will not work.
Then install it, before you log anything: on iPhone, Share, then Add to Home Screen; on Android, Install app from the menu.
On iPhone, the installed app keeps its data apart from Safari's.
The first screen asks you to protect your history.
Type a passphrase twice: at least ten characters, with a few different ones. Longer is better.
It makes the key that encrypts your store, and it is never written anywhere.
If you forget it, nobody can recover your data, so keep it in a password manager.
Next comes a short notice, shown only once.
The app is meant for adults, photo recognition is off by default, and your plates stay on this device, encrypted.
Tap Got it, and you're in.
Press Log, and choose Type it.
Search the food list on the device, which works offline, then pick a portion or type the grams.
Press Log again, and the plate lands on Today as a woven band, one stripe for each food group on it.
When you're done, Lock closes the store at once.
It also locks itself after fifteen idle minutes, or five minutes out of sight, and every visit starts with your passphrase.
Every step, with screenshots, is on the Getting started page of the docs.
